executiveSummary: Active targeting of Siemens S7-200/300/400/1200/1500 PLCs across multiple sectors has been confirmed by a U.S. joint advisory; actors leverage S7comm (TCP/102), open-source snap7 tooling, and poor segmentation. Immediate hardening, removal of internet exposure, and S7 protocol monitoring are required. Security Advisory Critical unauthenticated takeover vectors in Advantech industrial gateways (EKI-1242EIMS/IEIMS) and other IIoT components enable remote code execution, unsigned firmware upload, and OT service disruption; isolate devices, block management ports, and apply vendor updates as available. CISA Weekly Multiple Eclipse Milo (OPC UA) server flaws allow unauthorized method calls, diagnostics exposure, and resource exhaustion-posing direct risks to utilities and manufacturing when used as control data backbones. Enforce SignAndEncrypt, disable anonymous access, patch promptly, and segment brokers. CISA Weekly Pre-auth Brotli decoder flaws affect Siemens industrial/MES/PLM/IIoT software stacks (Node.js-bundled), exposing manufacturers to RCE/DoS via crafted compressed streams. Disable Brotli at proxies, patch Node.js/Brotli, and follow Siemens mitigations. ICS Advisory Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway vulnerabilities are under exploitation; appliances were used for initial access and web shelling in prior waves. Patch urgently, assume-breach if exposure overlapped exploit windows, and rotate credentials/secrets. CERT-FR Alert Edge/perimeter pressure persists: NGINX (HTTP/2) and a hardware-dependent Java runtime flaw ("Java4Shell") are driving scanning and exploit dev; apply vendor fixes, consider disabling HTTP/2 where possible, and monitor for abnormal worker crashes and long-lived HTTP/2 sessions. View Article View Article Widespread PHP zero-days with active exploitation continue to affect internet-facing portals; out-of-band security releases and WAF mitigations should be applied with urgency to reduce pivot paths toward OT environments. Security Advisory State-linked intrusion tradecraft remains focused on identity and edge infrastructure: China-nexus covert SOHO/IoT networks and Russian APT activity against Zimbra and router hygiene represent persistent enterprise entry points with OT pivot potential. relevance: The current period features multiple direct-to-OT risk items: active attempts to access Siemens S7 controllers (TCP/102), critical flaws in Advantech OT/IIoT gateways (including unauthenticated command execution and unsigned firmware acceptance), and exploitable conditions in OPC UA application stacks widely deployed in utilities and manufacturing. These issues materially increase the likelihood of operational disruption if internet exposure and IT-to-OT conduits are not tightly controlled. Edge and identity vectors remain the dominant enterprise entry points with credible OT pivot potential: NetScaler, SonicWall SSLVPN, and Zimbra exploitation persist, while high-severity flaws in NGINX, Java runtimes, and PHP expand the blast radius for web-facing assets supporting industrial operations. These conditions mandate rapid perimeter patching, strict segmentation (Purdue/IEC 62443), and active monitoring of ICS protocol traffic and engineering workstation activity.

Eclipse Milo (OPC UA) auth and resource flaws-patch, disable anonymous, enforce SignAndEncrypt. CISA Weekly
Advantech EKI gateways-auth bypass, RCE, unsigned firmware; isolate and patch. CISA Weekly

descriptions: Exploitation of public-facing applications and appliances (ATT&CK T1190): NetScaler, Zimbra, NGINX, Apache Roller.
Valid accounts, MFA abuse, and identity persistence (T1078, T1556): Zimbra app-specific passwords; cloud token abuse; VPN credential reuse.
Living-off-the-land (T1105/T1059/T1021): PsExec/WMI/WinRM for lateral movement; scheduled tasks; PowerShell.
Protocol abuse in OT (ATT&CK for ICS): Unauthorized S7comm reads/writes (TCP/102); OPC UA method calls and monitored item exhaustion.
Web supply-chain injection/data theft: third-party JS (Optimizely) with credential/cookie scraping and mobile exploit delivery.

outlook72h: Expect increased probing for NGINX HTTP/2 and fresh PHP vectors; tighten edge WAF and connection anomaly detections. OPC UA and S7 protocol scanning activity likely to continue; prioritize segmentation changes that can be implemented without downtime. Expedite NetScaler and VPN remediation/triage, including credential and token rotation across federated identity systems. For Siemens industrial software environments, rapidly disable Brotli at gateways and schedule Node.js/Brotli upgrades.
